_meta.source: Written for this app, grounded in Krumboltz planned happenstance theory and in the structure of the Singapore education and training system
_meta.notes: Chance cards are the engine of the Journey mode. Each fires at a life stage, and whether the player can use it is checked against dispositions, never against grades. A chance the player cannot use is never framed as a punishment. It is framed as something that happened while they were not looking, and it is always replayable. No card removes an option permanently. Situations and setbacks are written to be recognisable to a Singaporean student without being about any real person.

cards.title: A teacher stops you after class
cards.body: She says your last piece of work was the best thing she read that week, and asks whether you have thought about taking the subject further.
cards.ifTaken: You say yes, and she spends twenty minutes telling you what the subject actually leads to. You leave with two things you had never heard of.
cards.ifMissed: You say something polite and leave. She does not bring it up again, because teachers assume you know when you are not interested.

cards.title: Your school offers you a subject at a higher level
cards.body: Your results in one subject were strong enough that the school is offering to move it up a level next year. It will be harder and it will take more of your time.
cards.ifTaken: You take it. The first term is genuinely difficult and by the third you have caught up.
cards.ifMissed: You decline, which is a completely reasonable thing to do. The offer usually comes round again.

cards.title: You fail a paper badly
cards.body: Not a near miss. A genuinely bad result in a subject you thought you were fine in.
cards.ifTaken: You work out what actually went wrong instead of deciding you are bad at the subject. It takes a term to recover and you recover.
cards.ifMissed: You avoid the subject for a while. It stays uncomfortable for longer than it needed to.
onwardMoves: Ask the teacher to go through the paper with you
Move the subject to a level you can actually work at, which is not a defeat

cards.title: An open house you were not planning to attend
cards.body: A friend is going to a polytechnic and ITE open house and asks if you want to come. You had already decided that route was not for you.
cards.ifTaken: You go. You see a course you did not know existed and you find yourself asking questions for forty minutes.
cards.ifMissed: You stay home. You continue choosing between the four options you already knew about.

cards.title: The Early Admissions Exercise opens
cards.body: You can apply for a course on the strength of your interest and aptitude, before your results come out. It asks you to talk about what you have done and why you want this.
cards.ifTaken: You apply. Whether or not you get it, you have had to say out loud what you actually want, which turns out to be the hard part.
cards.ifMissed: You decide there is no point, because your results are not strong enough. The exercise was specifically designed not to work that way.

cards.title: Your results come out and you are short
cards.body: Not by much. By enough. The course you had in mind is not available to you this round.
cards.ifTaken: You take a route you had not been considering, because you looked properly at what it actually leads to rather than at what it sounds like.
cards.ifMissed: You take the nearest thing to your original plan without looking at the alternatives. It works out, more slowly.
onwardMoves: A fifth year, if you are eligible, to take subjects at a more demanding level
A foundation year inside the polytechnic
The ITE route, which reaches the same diploma by a different road

cards.title: Three months in, you know it is the wrong course
cards.body: Not too hard. Just not what you thought it was, and not what you want to spend three years on.
cards.ifTaken: You talk to someone, transfer or finish the year and switch. It costs you time and it does not cost you the decade.
cards.ifMissed: You finish it. The diploma is still a diploma and you find your way sideways afterwards, which large numbers of people do.
onwardMoves: Finish and switch field at the next step, which is extremely common
Use it as the base for something adjacent

cards.title: An internship nobody else applied for
cards.body: It is not glamorous and it is at a company you have never heard of. Your lecturer mentions it once.
cards.ifTaken: You take it. The company is small enough that you do real work, and the person supervising you remembers your name for the next ten years.
cards.ifMissed: You wait for a better one. Better ones are more competitive.

cards.title: Someone asks whether you can do something you have never done
cards.body: At work. In front of people. You could say yes and work it out, or say no and stay safe.
cards.ifTaken: You say yes. The first attempt is rough. You are now the person who does that thing.
cards.ifMissed: You say no, honestly, and someone else becomes the person who does that thing.

cards.title: Your employer will pay for you to upgrade
cards.body: Part time, alongside the job. It will cost you your evenings for two years.
cards.ifTaken: You do it. The two years are hard and at the end you hold a qualification you did not have at nineteen.
cards.ifMissed: You do not. The offer tends to come round again, and the SkillsFuture routes are there regardless of your employer.

cards.title: Your role disappears
cards.body: Not because of you. The work moved, or the company did, or the technology did.
cards.ifTaken: You treat it as a switch rather than an ending, and use the support that exists for exactly this.
cards.ifMissed: You look for the same job elsewhere for a while before widening. You get there, later.
onwardMoves: SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme, built for exactly this
From age 40, a $4,000 credit and a monthly training allowance while you retrain full time
A subsidised full time diploma, at up to 90 percent off, at any age

cards.title: Someone you worked with years ago calls
cards.body: They are building something and they thought of you. They thought of you because of how you were to work with, not because of your qualifications.
cards.ifTaken: You take the call, and then the meeting. It changes the next five years.
cards.ifMissed: You are busy. They call someone else who is also good.

cards.title: Your whole field changes underneath you
cards.body: The tools you built a career on are being replaced. Some of what you do can now be done in seconds by something else.
cards.ifTaken: You learn the new tools early, while it is still a choice rather than an emergency, and end up more valuable than before.
cards.ifMissed: You learn them later, under more pressure. You still learn them.
onwardMoves: Short courses using SkillsFuture Credit, on your own terms
A full reskilling with a training allowance from age 40
Move to the part of the field the change did not touch

cards.title: You could start again, properly
cards.body: There is a thing you have wanted to do for years. From 40 the state will pay most of the cost and give you an allowance while you study.
cards.ifTaken: You enrol. You are the oldest person in some of the rooms and it turns out that is not the problem you thought it would be.
cards.ifMissed: You keep going as you are, which is a real and reasonable choice. The programme does not expire.

cards.title: A younger person asks you how you got here
cards.body: They are where you were. They think their result decided everything.
cards.ifTaken: You tell them the real version, including the parts that went badly. They believe you because it does not sound like a speech.
cards.ifMissed: You give them the tidy version. It is less useful to them than the real one would have been.

cards.title: A small thing on the side
cards.body: Something you make, fix, sell, run or organise that nobody is grading. It takes your weekends.
cards.ifTaken: You keep at it. Years later it is the thing on your record that people ask about first.
cards.ifMissed: You let it go when it gets busy, which is what usually happens.
